title: Memory keepsake journal page
subtitle: A single-event layout that holds a photograph, a written memory, and physical ephemera on one page
excerpt: A memory keepsake journal page holds everything about one moment in one place: a photograph or printed image, a written account of a few sentences to a full paragraph, the date and location, and a small pocket or mount for a physical item such as a ticket stub, pressed flower, or paper wrapper. The design is one page per event, made to last rather than to be filled quickly.
sourceNotes: Memory keepsake journalling is a contemporary practice combining traditional scrapbooking and journalling. This entry is an original Homemade layout design.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small folded or glued paper pocket attached to a journal page that holds flat physical items (tickets, receipts, wrappers, pressed materials) without needing to glue the item itself to the page.

content.text: A memory keepsake page is a single document for a single moment. It is not a weekly spread or a rapid daily capture. It is made slowly, usually after the event, with the aim of being meaningful in 20 years. Each element (the image area, the written text, the date, the
) is placed for longevity, using archival-quality adhesives and acid-free materials.

items.name: Mixed-media journal, A5, with thick pages
items.notes: Pages of at least 200 gsm. Thin pages buckle under glue and mixed media elements. If the journal pages are thin, glue them together in pairs before use.

items.name: PVA adhesive, acid-free
items.notes: For mounting photographs and paper elements. PVA dries flexible. Avoid paste sticks (too brittle) and super glue (degrades paper).

items.name: Small paste brush
items.notes: For spreading PVA thinly and evenly.

items.name: Washi tape (optional)
items.notes: For attaching photograph corners without full-surface gluing, allowing the photograph to be removed later if needed.

content.text: Divide the page into three horizontal zones. Top zone (40% of page height): image area: a photograph or printed image mounted flush or with a small border. Middle zone (40% of page height): written text: date, location, and a few sentences to a paragraph describing the memory. Bottom zone (20% of page height): ephemera pocket and any labels. A simple page structure keeps the focus on the written memory rather than the decoration.

Cut a rectangle of card or thick paper 30 mm shorter than the page width and 40 to 50 mm tall. Fold up the bottom 10 mm to form the base of the pocket. Apply PVA to the outside of the left and right edges of the folded base section and press the pocket firmly onto the page in the bottom zone. The open top of the pocket remains unglued: this is where flat ephemera slides in and out. Washi tape along the left and right edges of the pocket reinforces the bond and also decorates.

items.symptom: The page buckles and warps after the photograph is glued in place
items.cause: The PVA adhesive has introduced moisture into one side of the page but not the other, causing differential swelling.
items.fix: Apply PVA in a thin, even layer. Close the journal and place under a heavy weight while the adhesive dries (at least 30 minutes). For very thin journal pages, back each page with a second sheet before mounting photographs.
